guides.vulnerability_name: Windows DNS Server Remote Code Execution
guides.treatment_action:
Recommended treatment actions:  
- Apply critical security patches for CVE-2020-1350 on SRV-01 and SRV-02 immediately  
- Disable unnecessary network services on all hosts, particularly non-essential protocols on SRV-03 and SRV-04  
- Implement firewall rules to restrict access to DNS (53), SMB (445), and WinRM (5985/5986) ports to authorized IP ranges  
- Configure web application firewalls on SRV-04 to mitigate risks from CVE-2021-44228  
- Enforce TLS 1.2+ encryption for all remote management interfaces (WinRM) across affected hosts  
- Conduct vulnerability scanning and penetration testing for network services per ISO 27002:2022 8.29  
- Deploy network segmentation to isolate domain controllers (SRV-01) from other hosts  
- Implement application layer filtering (ISO 27002:2022 8.23) to block malicious traffic patterns  
- Update application server configurations on SRV-04 to include input validation and output encoding  
- Establish baseline security configurations for all hosts using ISO 27002:2022 8.20 network security guidelines

implementation_steps.title: Verify DNS Service Status
implementation_steps.description: Check the current status of the DNS Server service to ensure it is running and configured correctly.
implementation_steps.expected_result: DNS service status shows 'Running' with a StartType of 'Automatic'.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the output of 'Get-Service -Name DNS' as a text file.

implementation_steps.title: Check Installed Patches for CVE-2020-1350
implementation_steps.description: Verify if the critical security patch for CVE-2020-1350 is installed on SRV-01.
implementation_steps.expected_result: The output displays the KB4556784 hotfix with installation date and status.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture the output of 'Get-HotFix' filtered for KB4556784 as a screenshot.

implementation_steps.title: Install Missing Security Patches
implementation_steps.description: Install the critical security update for CVE-2020-1350 using Windows Update.
implementation_steps.expected_result: The update completes successfully, and the system reboots if required.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the output of 'Install-WindowsUpdate' and confirm reboot logs.

implementation_steps.title: Restrict DNS Port (53) with Firewall Rules
implementation_steps.description: Create firewall rules to restrict access to DNS (port 53) to authorized IP ranges.
commands: New-NetFirewallRule -Name "DNS-TCP-Restricted" -DisplayName "DNS TCP Restricted" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 53 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow -RemoteIpAddress 192.168.1.0/24
New-NetFirewallRule -Name "DNS-UDP-Restricted" -DisplayName "DNS UDP Restricted" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 53 -Protocol UDP -Action Allow -RemoteIpAddress 192.168.1.0/24
implementation_steps.expected_result: Two new firewall rules named 'DNS-TCP-Restricted' and 'DNS-UDP-Restricted' are created with the specified IP range.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Export the firewall rules using 'Get-NetFirewallRule' and save as a CSV file.

implementation_steps.title: Disable Non-Essential Network Services
implementation_steps.description: Disable unnecessary network services (e.g., NetBIOS) to reduce attack surface.
implementation_steps.expected_result: The NetBT service startup type is set to 'Disabled' with status 'Stopped'.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Capture the output of 'Get-Service -Name NetBT' after modification.

implementation_steps.title: Enforce TLS 1.2 for WinRM
implementation_steps.description: Configure the registry to enforce TLS 1.2 for WinRM remote management.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Registry keys for TLS 1.2 under both Client and Server subkeys have 'Enabled' set to 1.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Export the registry keys using 'reg export' and save as a .reg file.

implementation_steps.title: Validate Firewall Rule Application
implementation_steps.description: Verify that the newly created DNS firewall rules are applied and active.
commands: Get-NetFirewallRule -Name "DNS-*" | Format-List Name, Enabled, Action, RemoteIpAddress
implementation_steps.expected_result: The rules 'DNS-TCP-Restricted' and 'DNS-UDP-Restricted' show 'Enabled' as 'True' with the correct IP range.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Save the output of 'Get-NetFirewallRule' as a text file.

implementation_steps.title: Review DNS Logs for Anomalies
implementation_steps.description: Check DNS server logs for any suspicious activity post-remediation.
implementation_steps.expected_result: The output displays recent DNS events with no errors or suspicious activity.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Export the DNS logs using 'Get-WinEvent' and save as a .evtx file.

guides.treatment_action:
Recommended treatment actions:  
- Apply security patches for CVE-2020-1350 on SRV-01 immediately to mitigate DNS Server RCE vulnerability  
- Implement network segmentation to isolate SRV-01 from non-essential network traffic  
- Disable or restrict WinRM access on SRV-03 to only trusted IP ranges and authenticated users  
- Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all remote access to SRV-03  
- Conduct regular access control reviews to ensure segregation of duties compliance for users accessing SRV-01 and SRV-03  
- Deploy web filtering solutions to block malicious domains and prevent unauthorized remote access attempts  
- Encrypt all removable storage media used for remote work and enforce strict media handling policies  
- Update remote work policies to include mandatory use of secure, approved remote access tools  
- Perform quarterly vulnerability scans on SRV-01 and SRV-03 to detect and remediate new exposures  
- Implement role-based access control (RBAC) to limit user permissions on SRV-01 and SRV-03 to the principle of least privilege

implementation_steps.description: Create a firewall rule to allow WinRM only from trusted IP ranges.
commands: New-NetFirewallRule -Name "WinRM-Restricted" -DisplayName "WinRM Restricted Access" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 5985 -Protocol TCP -RemoteIP 192.168.1.0/24 -Action Allow -Enabled True
implementation_steps.expected_result: Firewall rule 'WinRM-Restricted' is created and enabled.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Output of 'Get-NetFirewallRule -Name "WinRM-Restricted"'

implementation_steps.title: Verify WinRM Configuration
implementation_steps.description: Validate WinRM service configuration for encryption and access restrictions.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Display shows AllowUnencrypted=False and other secure settings.

implementation_steps.description: Apply patches for CVE-2021-31166 and related vulnerabilities.

implementation_steps.description: Export current firewall rules for compliance and audit purposes.

implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Copy of 'C:\FirewallRules\WinRM-Restricted.xml'

guides.treatment_action:
Recommended treatment actions:  
- Implement a configuration management tool (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) to enforce and automate secure logging configuration settings on SRV-04.  
- Conduct a manual and automated review of the application server's logging configuration to remove or disable unnecessary logging features (e.g., debug logs, verbose error messages).  
- Integrate logging configuration changes into the organization's technical vulnerability management process (control 8.8) for continuous monitoring and remediation.  
- Apply the principle of least privilege to logging configurations, restricting access to log files and ensuring only authorized personnel can modify or view them.  
- Document and enforce a change management process (control 8.32) for all configuration changes, including approvals, testing, and rollback procedures.  
- Perform regular configuration audits using tools like OpenSCAP or CIS benchmarks to ensure compliance with secure configuration standards.  
- Train system administrators and developers on secure configuration practices, including logging configuration best practices, as part of information security awareness programs (control 5.8).  
- Enable logging of all configuration changes on SRV-04 and store logs in a secure, tamper-evident location for audit and forensic purposes.  
- Update the application server's software and dependencies to address the CVE-2021-44228 vulnerability, ensuring compatibility with the secure logging configuration.  
- Establish a configuration baseline for application servers, including logging settings, and enforce it across all hosts in the environment.

implementation_steps.title: Install and configure Ansible for configuration management
implementation_steps.description: Install Ansible using Chocolatey and configure it to manage logging settings on SRV-04.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Ansible installed successfully with Windows module support.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Screenshot of successful installation and collection installation.

implementation_steps.title: Disable verbose logging in IIS
implementation_steps.description: Modify IIS logging settings to disable verbose error messages and debug logs.
implementation_steps.expected_result: IIS configured to use custom error responses instead of verbose messages.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Exported IIS configuration using appcmd list config "Default Web Site".

implementation_steps.title: Secure log file permissions
implementation_steps.description: Restrict access to log files using NTFS permissions.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Log directory permissions restricted to SYSTEM and Administrators, denying Users access.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Screenshot of icacls output and log directory security tab.

implementation_steps.title: Enable auditing for log directory changes
implementation_steps.description: Configure Windows auditing to track changes to log files.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Auditing enabled for object access and system events.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Audit policy configuration export using auditpol get /category:*.

implementation_steps.title: Apply CIS benchmark for Windows Server 2016
implementation_steps.description: Run OpenSCAP to audit and remediate configuration against CIS benchmarks.
commands: oscap xccdf eval --profile CIS Microsoft Windows Server 2016 Security Benchmark --remediate --results results.xml --report report.html
implementation_steps.expected_result: CIS benchmark scan completed with remediation applied.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Exported results.xml and report.html from OpenSCAP scan.

implementation_steps.title: Install security updates for CVE-2021-44228
implementation_steps.description: Check for and install Windows updates addressing the vulnerability.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Relevant security updates installed successfully.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Output from Get-HotFix showing installed KB numbers.

implementation_steps.title: Enable logging of configuration changes
implementation_steps.description: Configure Windows Event Log to track configuration changes via PowerShell.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Event log configured to store 1GB of configuration change events.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Screenshot of Event Viewer showing GroupPolicy logs.

implementation_steps.title: Document configuration baseline
implementation_steps.description: Export current configuration settings as a baseline for future audits.
implementation_steps.expected_result: Configuration baseline exported to XML and CIM files.
implementation_steps.evidence_capture: Hash of ConfigBaseline.xml and CIM file stored in secure repository.
